_comment: IWMP / Tadweer — green (real, presets/iwmp/theme.json). Ramp/secondary/success additions: figma-token-sync (docs/figma-color-extraction.md §1/§2) — Figma 'Tadweer' mode.

secondary-foreground-strong.$description: Same fix as uccp.tokens.json (designer report 2026-09-07, generic enum dot-chip legibility) — this tenant shares the identical `secondary` (#667085) solid-fill/white-text pairing, so it inherited the same latent bug (core's navy `secondary-foreground-strong` alias against a dark tenant `secondary` fill). Reuses this tenant's own `secondary-foreground` (white), mirroring the dark-theme mirror's own approach.

primary-400.$description: interpolated 300–500 midpoint; Figma source had 300/400 duplicated

success-text.$description: D-6 (filters SPEC I.80 — the motivating case: Tadweer's brand green `#22c882`/`#12b76a` is 2.18:1/2.62:1 on white, both fail 4.5:1 as text). Override slot NOT set to the core alias: IWMP has its OWN green brand ramp (success-scale-700 above, = this tenant's own primary-700), so its own step is used instead of core's generic success-scale.700 (#027a48) — same ramp position, tenant-correct hue. Measured 5.41:1 on white, 5.01:1 on this tenant's surface-secondary (#E9FAF3).

primary-text.$description: D-6 family, navbar parity: the AA-safe on-WHITE step of this tenant's brand ramp, used for the nav rail's ACTIVE row (a white chip carrying brand-coloured icon + label). Tadweer's brand green #22C882 is 2.18:1 on white and fails as text; this is the same ramp position as success-scale-700 / primary-700. 5.41:1 on white.

error-text.$description: D-6: explicit override slot, set to the CORE alias (color.error-text = error.700) — IWMP has no red/error ramp of its own (the `#f04438` red flagged in I.80 as 3.76:1/failing is the shared core `destructive`/`error` red, not a Tadweer-specific colour). 6.57:1 on white.

shellRailBg.$description: Outer app-rail background override (specs/navbar SPEC.md §3 — the designer's standalone navbar build: 170°, five stops, blue → green), read by SideNav via --shell-rail-bg. $type is nominally 'color' for shape-consistency with this file's other tokens; the value is a gradient, and this file is read directly by style-dictionary.config.js's buildTenantsCss() post-build action, not through the standard Style Dictionary color pipeline.
